what_it_does: Cloud data warehouses store enormous files (like Parquet, a compressed column-oriented data format) across many storage servers using a technique called erasure coding, which breaks each file into chunks spread across servers so data survives even if some servers fail. To speed up data analysis queries, engineers want to push filtering logic ('only give me rows where sales > 1000') down to the storage servers themselves rather than hauling all the raw data to a central query engine first. The problem is that erasure coding fragments file objects across servers in a way that makes it hard to evaluate filters locally — a storage server typically holds only a shard of a file, not a coherent slice, so it cannot filter without first reassembling the file across the network. Fusion redesigns both how data is laid out on disk and how pushdown queries are executed so that each storage server can evaluate predicates on its own local slice of data without needing to fetch pieces from other servers, eliminating the reassembly bottleneck.
